text:
Trevor Moore grew up in Thousand Oaks, went undrafted out of the University of Denver, won a Calder Cup with the Toronto Marlies and has spent most of his career as the Kings' reliable second-tier scorer. This season fits the pattern so far: five goals in 21 games, four of them in his last ten, including the go-ahead goal in Montreal on November 23 in his first game back from a short absence.

His finishing looks honest. Five goals on 3.99 expected, an 11.1% shooting percentage, and a talent range that says about 11% is who he is. His points rate (1.43 per 60) is a little below last season's.

The worry is the five-on-five share. Los Angeles has 44.9% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) with him on the ice, and his relative number is more than six points below his teammates. That's a big change for a player Evolving-Hockey rated 144th among 401 forwards last season. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had 59% of his shots coming off the rush, so when the Kings play in transition, he tends to show up. Watch his line's chance share more than his goals.
